title: A pooled runoff shape ratio above one did not establish extra wet-year loss in 175 Australian catchments
abstract: We audit a claim that runoff loss grew faster than flow in wet years after 1997. We prove that the pooled slope-to-offset ratio can exceed one under exact proportional changes at every catchment, because the two components use different weights. An exact two-catchment example gives 2.143. In the published Fu-model results for 175 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021, the observed ratio is 1.567, while fitted proportional responses on the same predictor years give 1.282. We subtract this benchmark and test the remaining slope-minus-offset contrast. The estimate is -3.73 percentage points. Its spatial-only 95% interval is -7.88 to +1.41; a paired spatial and three-year temporal block interval is -13.72 to +6.45. The SILO rain check also includes zero. The pooled ratio therefore did not establish extra wet-year loss. This does not remove the persistent runoff deficit or prove proportionality. The test reuses published predictions, holds calibration fixed and has only 12 late test years. Code, proof, input hashes, all draws and independent numerical checks are supplied.

display.caption: The corrected extra-shape contrast includes zero under all five uncertainty schemes. The published pooled ratio exceeds one even for fitted proportional responses on the same predictors.

citations.reason: Uses published Fu predictions and reference statistics; challenges the interpretation of a pooled ratio above one as extra wet-year loss.
